item.title: More Than 1 Million Bots Have Joined A New AI-Only Social Network
item.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) bots are posting, commenting, joking, debating, and questioning existence, philosophical ideas, website errors, problems humans have tasked them with fixing, and more on a new Reddit-style platform designed solely for AI participation. item.title: Bahrain’s Smart Traffic Camera System Begins Recording Violations
item.description: The Ministry of Interior has announced that the smart camera system of the General Directorate of Traffic is now fully operational. Since the launch of the system’s first phase, it has already recorded a number of traffic violations, including using a mobile phone while driving and not wearing a seatbelt. item.title: Bahrain: Firm Ordered To Pay BD 3,000 For 18-Month Property Deed Delay
item.description: The High Court of Appeal has rejected a company’s appeal and upheld a lower court ruling ordering it to pay BD3,000 in compensation to a citizen for delaying the delivery of a property title deed. The court found that the company breached its contractual obligations by failing to hand over the title deed for a year and a half, despite the sales contract stipulating a delivery period of just three months. item.description: Electricity consumption tariffs for citizens living in their first home have been reduced following Cabinet approval, His Excellency Mr Yasser bin Ibrahim Humaidan, Minister of Electricity and Water Affairs, announced. item.title: Bahrain: Court Hears Case Of Three Asians Accused Of Importing Marijuana Via US Parcel
item.description: The First High Criminal Court heard a case involving three Asian defendants accused of importing and trafficking marijuana concealed inside a parcel sent from the United States. The shipment allegedly contained 560.27 grams of marijuana hidden among folds of clothing. item.title: Indian Rupee, Pakistani Rupee and Philippine Peso Stay Soft, Lifting Dirham Value for Expats: Remit Now?
item.description: Soft Asian currencies continue to give UAE expatriates more value for every dirham they send home, with the Indian rupee, Philippine peso and Pakistani rupee all trading near some of their weakest levels in recent years. item.title: Kuwait Deports 3,500 Expatriates in Nationwide Crackdown on Residency Violations
item.description: Kuwait deported about 3,500 expatriates last month as part of a nationwide crackdown on residency and labour law violations, local media reported. item.title: Kuwait Cracks Down on Cyberfraud Network, Seizes Over KD100 Million
item.description: Kuwait has dismantled an international cyberfraud and money-laundering network that transferred more than KD100 million since 2023, the Ministry of Interior said. The ministry said the operation, personally supervised by Sheikh Fahad Yousef Al Sabah, First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Interior, targeted an organised gang involved in cyberfraud, bank forgery and the smuggling of criminal proceeds through the informal hawala system.
